Treatment requires 2–4 weeks of intravenous antibiotics in the acute phase, followed by 3–6 months of oral therapy. Preventive measures include waterproofing, protective footwear, masks, boiled water, and thorough hand hygiene.

articleSummary: Seasonal influenza spreads more in cold weather and crowded indoor spaces in Vietnam, including schools, offices, and public transport. Severe cases may require intensive care, mechanical ventilation, renal replacement therapy, and even ECMO; a young patient requiring ventilation, dialysis, and ECMO is cited. Two routes to severity: in older or comorbid patients, influenza destabilizes chronic diseases (heart disease, COPD, diabetes) leading to myocardial infarction, stroke, pneumonia, sepsis, and death; in otherwise healthy individuals, the virus can directly injure multiple organs (myocarditis, pericarditis). Do not use antibiotics or corticosteroids; seek care for fever lasting >48 hours, chest pain, or shortness of breath, and avoid aspirin-containing medicines due to Reye syndrome.

articleSummary: Knowlesi malaria reappears in Taiwan after 15 years. A Taiwanese woman in her 50s who traveled to Malaysia’s tropical rainforest regions in late July did not take malaria prophylaxis and was bitten by insects. This marks Taiwan’s first domestically linked Knowlesi malaria case since 2005, with health authorities monitoring the patient closely. Knowlesi malaria is a Southeast Asian parasite with reported cases in Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand, Singapore, Vietnam, Myanmar, and Indonesia; symptoms typically arise 7–30 days post-infection and can resemble influenza. Severe disease can include splenomegaly, jaundice, shock, organ failure, pulmonary edema, or cerebral malaria; vivax and malariae infections may relapse, warranting Primaquine after blood-stage treatment. By September 14, 2026, Taiwan recorded 6 imported malaria cases (Ethiopia 2, Pakistan 1, Nigeria 1, Malaysia 1, others 1); 71 imported malaria cases since 2017, mainly falciparum and vivax. Public health guidance emphasizes pre-travel consultation, continuous chemoprophylaxis, mosquito precautions, and prompt post-travel medical attention with travel history.

articleSummary: TB mortality in Brazil shows spatial inequalities across 5570 municipalities from 2010 to 2024, with 73,432 TB-related deaths. articleSummary: After rain, African giant snails (Achatina fulica) have appeared in Guangdong, China, posing ecological and public-health threats. The species is listed among the 100 worst invasive species and on China’s key invasive-species list. These snails carry Angiostrongylus cantonensis (Guangzhou rat lungworm), with infection rates in Guangzhou and Shenzhen of 27%–41% and averages over 150 parasites per snail. The parasite can invade the central nervous system or cerebrospinal fluid, causing meningitis and potentially fatal illness. Reproduction is rapid (30–700 eggs per snail), threatening over 500 plant species. Prevention: do not touch or handle, and do not eat. articleHeadline: Is Applying A Small Drop Of Citronella Oil Effective Against Dengue?
articleSummary: Seasonal dengue surges in India during the monsoon, driven by Aedes aegypti, are not halted by a single drop of citronella oil. Citronella can repel mosquitoes, but a lone drop provides a tiny, short-lived barrier that evaporates within minutes, leaving most of the body exposed; reapplication every 30–60 minutes is often required. Field conditions—heat, wind, and sweat—undermine lab knockdown efficacy, making citronella a limited, transient protection. Compared with DEET, picaridin, or oil of lemon eucalyptus, it should not be relied upon to prevent dengue. A multi-layer defense is advised: apply EPA/WHO-approved repellents on exposed skin during peak Aedes activity (early morning, late afternoon); wear light, protective clothing; eliminate stagnant water; install barrier nets and screens. Safety note: undiluted citronella can cause skin irritation; dilution is essential.

articleHeadline: 安徽：重大传染病疫情首发首报人员最高奖励1万元
articleSummary: Anhui Province, China, issued pilot rules to reward the first reporters of major infectious disease outbreaks to boost early detection and response. On September 15, the Anhui Health Commission, Anhui CDC, and Anhui Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine issued the Implementation Rules for First Reporting and Notification of Major Infectious Disease Outbreaks (Trial). The rules designate eligible reporters—including medical and health institutions, third-party testing laboratories, and their staff—for timely discovery and reporting of major outbreaks. Applicable diseases cover Class A infectious diseases (and Class B diseases under Class A controls), newly emerging infections, outbreaks of unknown origin, and reemergence of eliminated diseases. A closed-loop workflow is defined: national praise, municipal CDC verification, provincial review of first reporters, national re-review, and provincial publication and awarding. Rewards: individuals receive 10,000 yuan for first global or China-first major outbreak; 8,000 yuan for outbreaks of plague, SARS, anthrax, smallpox, polio, or other major diseases.

articleHeadlineTranslated: Eastern DRC: four months after the start of the Ebola outbreak, authorities hail a slight improvement.
articleHeadline: Est de la RDC: quatre mois après le début de l'épidémie d'Ebola, les autorités saluent une légère amélioration
articleSummary: Four months after the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo was declared on May 15, authorities report a slowing transmission. On September 12, Health Minister Samuel Kamba said the peak had passed and transmission since mid-August has slowed from about 120 to roughly 80 cases per day. AU health authorities note improvements in some areas; in Ituri province, three health zones Adja, Kambala and Mahagi have had no new cases in 41 days. But the World Health Organization cautions that national trends mask local variation. In Nord-Kivu, the outbreak is expanding exponentially, notably in Butembo, with weekly case counts rising from about 100 to over 200 and the province now accounting for about 45% of weekly total. Sud-Ubangi has become the seventh province affected, highlighting geographic spread amid high mobility. The WHO says 5,000 more health workers are needed; there is no licensed vaccine or treatment for Bundibugyo.
notes: 発生地域にChad（Guera Region等）が含まれるが、記事本文はDRC（Ituri、Nord-Kivu、Sud-Ubangi）のエボラ流行のみを扱っており、Chadは無関係のため除外した。WHOは5,000人の追加医療従事者が必要と指摘、ワクチン・治療薬未承認のBundibugyo種である点も重大。

articleSummary: Vas County saw campylobacteriosis (3 cases) and salmonellosis (6 cases) predominate among infectious diseases in the Sept 1–6 reporting week, with three suspected scarlet fever confirmed. Nationally, Aug 31–Sep 6 did not trigger a mass gastroenteritis outbreak. A 79-year-old man in Pest County was suspected of tetanus and received active tetanus vaccination after hospital admission. A 6-year-old boy in Bács-Kiskun County, previously vaccinated, had suspected parotitis epidemica (mumps) with diagnostics ongoing. An imported viral hemorrhagic fever case was reported: a 43-year-old man in Pest County tested positive for Dengue virus after travel in the Philippines. A domestically acquired West Nile fever case was reported in an 83-year-old man in the capital, bringing 2026 total to four, with most patients male and aged 60–83; all had neurological symptoms and were hospitalized. Mpox was diagnosed in a 48-year-old man in the capital and a 23-year-old man in Győr-Moson-Sopron County; neither had mpox vaccination.

articleHeadline: Kasus Influenza Melonjak di Surabaya, Ruang Anak hingga IGD Sejumlah RS Dikabarkan Sempat Penuh
articleSummary: Influenza cases surged in Surabaya, East Java, with pediatric wards and emergency departments in several hospitals reported full. Most patients are children; the surge has lasted about a week. At RS Husada Utama Surabaya, CEO Dr. Didi Dewanto said pediatric units were full, with one floor housing 44 beds filled and rooms repurposed. Other facilities reported similar strain, while RS Kemenkes Surabaya (Class A) did not see a significant uptick. Public health officials urged hygiene, healthy living, and influenza vaccination; lab confirmation of virus variant was not yet available. Dinkes Kota Surabaya head Billy Daniel Messakh attributed a mild rise in fever to weather changes and increased activity, noting most influenza cases are treated as outpatients, with severe cases prioritized. The public is advised to verify information and seek care at Puskesmas if needed.

articleSummary: Overseas wild birds have driven a surge in highly pathogenic avian influenza, while neighboring China and Mongolia report a new SAT1-type foot-and-mouth disease outbreak, prompting South Korea to designate October–February as a special prevention period. The measures: expanded migratory-bird alerts, 280 access-control zones, and drone-assisted disinfection of sanctuaries. Farm biosecurity tightens to a three-tier system, with large layer farms adopting a four-tier entry regime—vehicles and workers must be pre-registered seven days prior—and about 100 CCTV-equipped unmanned checkpoints. From 2027, the AX integrated quarantine package will unify entry control, disinfection, records, early detection, and smart diagnostics. ASF detections reached 197 in Jan–Aug, with new cases in Ulsan and Goryeong; 150 traps, 64 slaughterhouses, and 36 plasma-feed samples will be tested. Border checks and worker training expand; hotspots include Hwacheon, Chuncheon, Chungju, Pocheon, and Gapyeong.
